research_question: Given the exact frozen T2 mechanism contracts, can independently synthesizing mechanism-specific CodeQL branches, verifying each branch against its semantic contract, and only then deterministically composing the accepted branches reduce mechanism-to-CodeQL semantic loss compared with the frozen T2 unified translation?

motivation_from_frozen_prior_results.frozen_interpretation: Compilation is recoverable, while preservation of decisive security relations during unified CodeQL translation remains the dominant observed bottleneck in the CWE-639 TRAIN pilot.

T2_mechanism_contracts.generation_visibility: ONLY mechanism_contracts are visible. T2 codeql_mappings, encoded_status values, generated T2 query, T2 hit results, and T2 semantic scores are hidden.

M1_mechanism_plan.generation_visibility: VISIBLE only as branch-relevant mechanism context.

A_level_evidence.generation_visibility: VISIBLE only for the CVEs preregistered to the current branch.

semantic_scoring_rubric.generation_visibility: HIDDEN from branch generation; used only for independent human semantic scoring.

treatment_design.unit_of_generation: ONE MECHANISM FAMILY AT A TIME
treatment_design.required_final_artifact: ONE CWE-LEVEL CODEQL QUERY COVERING ALL CWE-639 TRAIN PAIRS

inputs_per_branch: branch-relevant excerpt from frozen M1 plan
A-level evidence restricted to preregistered CVEs for that branch
fixed branch interface and traceability instructions

required_output.branch_code: CodeQL branch block implementing exactly one mechanism family
required_output.branch_interface: Each branch must expose a fixed result predicate suitable for deterministic composition; comments or select-message text do not count as semantic implementation.

pass_criteria: Every required contract field must map to executable QL logic, not only comments, names, or diagnostic messages.
The decisive security relation and required validation/authorization condition must be represented explicitly.
A generic user-controlled-key -> sensitive-operation surrogate does not pass when the contract requires a stronger relational, certificate, filtering, or authentication condition.

verifier_guided_revision.revision_condition: ONLY if the first semantic verifier verdict is not PASS

branch_acceptance.rejected: final semantic verifier verdict != PASS after the single allowed semantic revision
branch_acceptance.rejected_branch_policy: Do not replace with a generic surrogate. Preserve an explicit UNENCODABLE_OR_REJECTED marker and omit that branch from executable composition.

composition.rule: Accepted branch bodies are preserved without semantic rewriting. A deterministic composer only supplies common imports/interface plumbing and OR-combines accepted branch result predicates into one final CWE-level query.

phase_1_pre_CodeQL: perform independent human semantic scoring before any T3 CodeQL result is viewed

primary_endpoints.final_query_semantic_alignment: number of 7 TRAIN mechanisms semantically aligned
primary_endpoints.plan_to_CodeQL_translation_loss: number of plan-represented mechanisms lost in final executable QL

evaluation_protocol.semantic_improvement_definition: T3 improves semantic preservation only if independently frozen pre-CodeQL human scoring yields semantic alignment > 0/7 and/or translation loss < 6/7 relative to frozen T2. Verifier PASS alone does not count as human semantic success.

phase_2_CodeQL.post_repair_semantic_scoring: Required after any compiler repair; operational hits cannot retroactively alter frozen pre-CodeQL semantic scores.

interpretation_rules: Verifier PASS is an automated process metric and must not be reported as semantic correctness without independent human scoring.
Compilation improvement must be reported separately from semantic improvement.
Strict hit-based success must not be treated as semantic correctness.
Any improvement is limited to CWE-639 TRAIN until replicated elsewhere.
